content: RECEIPT PASS DATA FORMAT — design proposal surfaced 2026-05-21 in cross-model exchange (ChatGPT carrying, Gemini 3.5 Flash as skeptical verifier). Each claim emitted by a stack node is a structured JSON object with fixed fields: claim, evidence_type (enum: observed/derived/inferred/metaphorical/unverified), evidence_refs (logs/commits/doc sections or 'none'), confidence (0.0-1.0 with forced reason above 0.8), falsification_path, dependencies. Three drift-prevention constraints: (a) each pass runs in fresh context window — Independent Pass output parsed into schema by separate parser node before any other model sees it, so models never see each other's raw prose during Independent Pass; (b) Dissent Pass receives only structured claims, not original justifying prose, which strips stylistic priming; (c) schema vocabulary is fixed and small — models choose from enumerated evidence_type values rather than generating their own taxonomy each turn (which is where drift compounds). The format becomes the discipline: if a node cannot fit a claim into the schema, that is itself signal — usually metaphor pretending to be mechanism. Status: design hypothesis. Not yet implemented in stack. Companion to the 5-layer pipeline (independent → dissent → receipt → drift check → human adjudication) and Gemini's Asymmetric Honey-Pot Protocol MVT. Honey-pot test as currently described has known limitations: adversary-design problem (payload designer knows the flaw, so test grades calibration not non-sycophancy) and human-in-the-loop single point of failure (Anthony is currently the only adversary capable of catching meta-level sycophancy). Both tracked as separate open threads.
